name: Shook Ones
label: Revelation
lede: Shook Ones sold their first Revelation covers at a basement show in Ballard, came home from four weeks in Europe to lost jobs and a dead phone, and walked away from the label in 2007. A decade on, they went back to Revelation with a record every member wrote.

eras.title: Bellingham, by way of the Velvet Elvis
eras.text: Scott Freeman grew up at all-ages shows in Seattle, at the Velvet Elvis, RKCNDY and DV8. By 2004 he had a band in Bellingham, a demo and a fast, tuneful hardcore sound that Revelation heard within two years.

years.h: Scott Freeman starts Shook Ones in Bellingham, Washington
years.p: Freeman, the singer, spends 2003 and 2004 laying groundwork, then gets the band going in Bellingham. A demo comes first.

yt: Please Read / Bird On Ice, live at HMS, 2021
years.h: Sixteen gives Shook Ones a debut on Endwell Records
years.p: The band's first full-length comes out on Endwell Records.
years.xp: In 2021 Revelation marked a repress of Sixteen and The Unquotable A.M.H. with a band-made performance video, Please Read and Bird On Ice, filmed live at HMS.

eras.title: Too hands off
eras.text: Revelation gave Shook Ones two records and no rules, and the band spent the freedom on the road: the US, Japan, and almost four weeks in Europe. By November 2007 they were gone from the label.

years.h: Sixty tour covers end up at a basement show in Ballard
years.p: Shook Ones' first Revelation 7" was meant to ship with 60 special tour covers. After delays, Revelation says, they became release-show covers, sold in a Ballard basement.
years.xp: The first press was 300 on pink and 700 on purple. The 7" was repressed on white, and again in 2012 on green.

years.src: Scene Point Blank · Revelation Records · No Echo
years.h: Facetious Folly Feat is tracked and mixed in four days
years.p: Shook Ones' second album, and their only full-length on Revelation, goes down fast. The first press comes in yellow/brown split, red/yellow sunburst and red.
years.xp: The album is REV 142. Its year is not in Revelation's own pressing list, so the date here follows No Echo and Scene Point Blank, which both place it in 2006.

years.cap: Shook Ones live at KTUB, April 2008
years.h: Shook Ones go to Japan in April 2007
years.p: The band plays Japan that spring. Around these years they also put out a split with the Japanese band Easel.

years.h: Four weeks in Europe, and the jobs back home are gone
years.p: On a European tour of nearly four weeks, band members lose their jobs at home and have a cell phone shut off for lack of money, Freeman told Redefine.
years.xp:
Freeman was matter-of-fact about it: "A few of the guys lost their jobs and someone's cell phone got turned off because they don't have money."

Redefine's piece does not give the year of the tour. It is placed in 2007 here, between the Japan trip in April and the exit from Revelation in November.

q: hands off, but almost too hands off
years.h: Shook Ones walk away from Revelation
years.p: The band leaves in November, one of several to go between 2005 and 2007. Freeman says Revelation never did anything shady. The money just went to mail order first.
years.xp: Freeman's full verdict to Redefine: "They never pulled any weird shit... they were very hands off, but, like, almost too hands off."

years.cap: Shook Ones at The Hickey Underworld, April 5, 2009
yt: Order Form, live at El Corazon, Seattle, 2007
years.h: Vinnie Fiorello's answer to the studio bill: "Okay, invoice me"
years.p: The Unquoteable A.M.H. comes out on Paper + Plastick, run by [[Less Than Jake|e54e065f-0ce6-4779-9a9a-afd7b997471f]] drummer Vinnie Fiorello. The band spent twelve days in the studio, after a 2008 split with End of a Year on Runner Up.
years.xp:
Freeman told Redefine the band "did whatever we wanted with whoever we wanted," and Fiorello's reply was "Okay, invoice me." He described the label's approach as wanting to "put out records that I think are awesome."

The split-EP song Order Form is about gay rights. "The content has gotten attention from people, and it's good attention," Freeman said. The video is a live take from Seattle's El Corazon, opening for Lifetime in September 2007, two years before the album.

eras.title: A band that never broke up
eras.text: Shook Ones never announced a breakup. They put out a few singles in 2013, went quiet, then spent more than a year on a record that every member wrote, and took it back to Revelation.

yt: Carms Race, live at the Vera Project, Seattle, Dec 2015
years.h: After the 2013 singles, five years of nothing
years.p: Shook Ones release a few singles, then no new music until 2018. They never announce a breakup.

years.h: Body Feel starts on the Fourth of July
years.p: Drums and bass go down at Hear Me Shimmer and the Loom Room. Everyone writes, including members who don't play guitar.
years.xp:
Freeman said the record did not start as an assignment: "We weren't just like, 'Oh, we gotta write a new record.' We all write music and it's part of how we operate in our daily lives."

Bo Stewart said they had more than ten songs to pick from, a first for the band. The whole process took over a year.

years.src: No Echo · Revelation Records · Scene Point Blank
years.h: Body Feel brings Shook Ones back to Revelation
years.p: Their first album in nearly a decade is mixed and mastered by Jack Shirley at Atomic Garden. No Echo premieres Night Blind.
years.xp: Revelation had put out Facetious Folly Feat in 2006. Scene Point Blank says engineer Jackson Long recorded Aaron O'Neil and Bo Stewart playing live together, and the guitars were tracked one at a time, on each member's own schedule.

years.h: Bellingham gets the Body Feel release show
years.p: Shook Ones play the hometown release show for Body Feel, in Bellingham, Washington.
